chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the time of Maghrib, and he said: Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم for every salat with two times, except the salat of Maghrib, for indeed its time is one, and its time is its moment of obligation.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and what we have previously presented of the reports that this salat has two times, an earlier and a later one, and that its beginning is the disappearance of the sun and its end is the disappearance of the twilight. This is because the meaning in these two reports is what we mentioned earlier: namely, informing about the nearness between the two times, and that there is not between them the expansiveness that exists between the two times in the other prayers. If a person were to proceed calmly in his salat and perform it with deliberation, his completion of it would be at the disappearance of the twilight; thus, the two times are as though one time, due to the narrowness of what lies between them. And that which also indicates this is...

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: the angel Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام who conveyed the prayer times
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةُ الشَّمْسِ: the setting or disappearance of the sun
key_terms.وَقْتِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the prescribed time of Maghrib salat
key_terms.وُجُوبُهَا: the moment when it becomes obligatory

ai.seo_question: Why is the time of Maghrib salat described as one time in hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the time of Maghrib salat and states that, unlike the other prayers, its time is described as one. The accompanying explanation clarifies that this does not negate reports describing a beginning and end for its time; rather, the interval between them is so short that they are treated as though they were one.
